title: Which leg is missing?
intro: Every portfolio compromise has a signature. Diagnose which of the three legs each situation gave up.

buckets.label: Valuation missing
buckets.hint: Great record, price already assumed it

cards.text: ROC above 40%, beloved brand — and a flat decade as the market matured
Exceptional margins in a category that stopped expanding
A dominant lubricant maker with EVs slowly capping its future
RoE above 15% every year since 2006 — bought at a price that assumed it continues forever
The obviously wonderful franchise everyone already owns at 60× earnings
Revenue doubling yearly, funded by debt, in a business with no pricing power
A 5× P/E turnaround whose margins have never survived a downcycle
The hot smallcap growing 50% with promoter pledging climbing alongside

debrief: Each compromise has a distinct failure mode: growth-missing holdings (Castrol, Colgate) persist respectably and never compound — you lose to time; valuation-missing holdings (the HDFC Bank lesson) deliver the business performance you expected and still disappoint — you lose to the entry price; quality-missing holdings win the backtest and lose the drawdown — you lose to fragility, usually all at once. The audit's point: everyone claims to want all three, and most give one up without noticing. Find yours.
